title: ML-DSA-65 signing + verification of claim and handoff payloads
description:
Symphony reads the agent identity via GET /agent and signs claim and handoff payloads through a thin x0xd-side endpoint POST /agent/sign (which holds the agent key). Verification on read; mismatches drop the record with a WARN log. BLOCKED on x0x adding POST /agent/sign — track the corresponding x0x-side issue and link here when filed.

DESIGN CONTRACT (2026-07-02): Sign via POST /agent/sign with context x0x-symphony-claim-v1 (claims) / x0x-symphony-handoff-v1 (handoffs). x0xd signs the canonical DST [0xF0]|magic|x0x.external-agent-sign.v1|len(u32 BE)|context|payload; symphony reproduces it exactly for POST /agent/verify. Envelope stored at sign time: signature_b64 + algorithm (x0x.agent-sign.v2.ml-dsa-65) + context + public_key_b64. WHAT IS SIGNED: the exact stored payload bytes (XSY-0017 coupling rule) — never a re-derived canonical projection. Verify-on-read via /agent/verify; unsigned/mismatched dropped with WARN (design §11). Verify MUST confirm the envelope public_key belongs to the claiming agent, not merely that the signature is valid. HARD GATE: WP-3-style adversarial review before merge — context cross-replay, payload substitution, envelope public-key swap, truncation/extension, algorithm downgrade/null, replay across issue-ids, signer/claim-owner mismatch, invalid base64, oversized payload, x0xd-down, verify-endpoint mismatch.

title: Unsigned/invalid claim hides the whole issue from candidate lists
description: M3 audit lower finding on XSY-0020 (non-blocking). Under M2's no-process-boundary threat model an unsigned/signature-invalid claim causes the whole issue to be dropped from async read candidate lists (Required mode drops invalid records with WARN). Acceptable for M2 (all work local, no hostile records). Matters once records are network-sourced at M3: a single bad claim on an otherwise-valid issue hides the entire issue, and a network actor could suppress work by attaching a bad signature. At M3, decide whether to drop only the offending claim (issue stays visible) rather than the whole issue, and surface the bad-claim event explicitly. Not a blocker for M2/M3-network-off.

title: Explicit cross-version additive-schema-vs-signature survival test
description: M3 audit lower finding on XSY-0020 (non-blocking). The additive-schema rule says a future optional field must not break existing signatures. The invariant is documented (issue.rs # Schema freeze and signatures) and the mechanism is sound, but NO single test currently bridges the two: byte-stability tests cover issues (not signed claims/handoffs), and the 11 signing adversarial tests cover signature attacks (not schema evolution). Add an explicit test: v1-signed claim/handoff, introduce a v2 optional field that is absent, assert the v1 signature still verifies under the v2 reader.

title: Red-team LOWs: workspace dir perms/umask + newline rejection in env values + boundary tests
description: Deferred from XSY-0040 item (d). title: Signed ApprovalEvent/DenialEvent types + content-hash binding + TTL expiry
description: ADR-0005 (amended 2026-07-03). ApprovalEvent/DenialEvent/ApprovalConsumed data types. Binding key = issue_id + canonical content-hash + signer (NOT claim_id; claim_id is audit-only). ApprovalEvent {issue_id, content_hash, signer_agent_id, verdict: Approve|Deny, approved_at, approver_agent_id, signature, claim_id (audit-only)}. Canonical content-hash = deterministic hash of issue payload (title/body/commands) at approval time. Payload change -> content_hash mismatch -> approval void -> re-PendingApproval. ApprovalConsumed {issue_id, content_hash, signer_agent_id, nonce, consumed_at, signature} records single-execution consumption; gate treats a consumed approval as invalid. Denial is terminal for the issue's network dispatch until payload changes (new hash = re-eligible). Signed via x0x-symphony-signing / x0xd identity (reuse ML-DSA-65 envelope). TTL expiry: expired approval = re-gate. Persisted in CRDT KvStore so restart re-verifies. Verify-on-read: signature valid AND content_hash matches current payload AND not expired AND no matching ApprovalConsumed exists. Pure event structs + deterministic hash in core; signing/verify helpers in signing layer (avoid core->signing cycle). Data layer only; no dispatch wiring (XSY-0050).

title: Cryptographic approval verification in dispatch gate (prerequisite for XSY-0051 REST API)
description: Security finding from advisor review of XSY-0050: the dispatch gate treats an ApprovalEvent as valid via ApprovalEvent::is_valid() which only checks signature_envelope_is_consistent() (self-referential SHA-256 over algorithm/context/signer/payload-hash). That is a data-layer consistency check, NOT a cryptographic ML-DSA-65 signature verification. The approval.rs is_valid doc explicitly says callers with a SigningClient must cryptographically verify before treating Valid as executable consent. XSY-0050's approval_gate_decision does NOT do this. Under Approve policy, anyone with write access to the approval store could forge a locally-consistent envelope and execute a network-sourced issue. FIX: wire SigningClient + TrustedKeyResolver (from x0x-symphony-signing) into the orchestrator. In approval_gate_decision, before treating an ApprovalEvent/DenialEvent as executable consent, cryptographically verify its signature (verify the event signing_payload_bytes against the APPROVER's public key, resolved via TrustedKeyResolver::resolve(approver_agent_id), under APPROVAL_CONTEXT). An event whose is_valid()==Valid but fails crypto-verify MUST be treated as invalid (not executable). ApprovalConsumed (local attestation, XSY-0050) stays as-is: it is an audit/spend record, not operator consent, and local attestation is acceptable for it. This is a prerequisite for XSY-0051 (REST approval API) because the REST handler must sign ApprovalEvents via x0xd and the gate must verify them the same way.
acceptance: Orchestrator holds optional SigningClient + TrustedKeyResolver (injected alongside trust_client)
approval_gate_decision cryptographically verifies each ApprovalEvent/DenialEvent signature before treating as executable consent

Crypto-verified valid approval executes and writes ApprovalConsumed (XSY-0050 single-execution preserved)
